mainTopic: Acts that take effect later: רבי יוחנן's 'in his hands' rule, תרומה on growing produce, and transferring what does not exist yet
overview: רבי יוחנן holds that if the thing a later קידושין depends on is fully in a person's own hands (בידו), the קידושין can work. The גמרא explains why this does not help a man who says 'after I convert': a גר needs three judges, and he cannot make them come. It then defends the rule against two challenges. A freed שפחה becomes a completely new person, and after a divorce, remarrying needs the woman's consent. An attempt to use this to settle רב אושעיא's question about two פרוטות is pushed back. A ברייתא about separating תרומה from produce still attached 'when it is detached' supports רבי יוחנן. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב goes further and allows produce that has not yet reached a third of its growth. רבה and רב יוסף argue how far his rule reaches, in two versions, and the גמרא applies each version to betrothing an unborn daughter. Finally אביי says that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי, and רבי מאיר all hold that a person can transfer something not yet in the world, and the proof for רבי begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Why conversion is not 'in his hands'
steps.stepSummary: A גר needs a בית דין of three, and he cannot be sure three will agree to sit for him. So conversion is not fully in his control.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גר needs three people. Why? The תורה calls it 'law', so it is like a court case. And who says these three will agree to deal with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן's 'in his hands' rule does not save the case of 'be betrothed to me after I convert'. Conversion depends on three other people, not on him alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule only works when a person controls the outcome by himself. Because conversion needs a בית דין of three, and he cannot force them to come, the conversion is not 'in his hands'. So his קידושין before converting does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Law or judgment, the kind a court decides

phrases.english: A convert requires three.
phrases.notes: Three judges, a small בית דין.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
'Law' is written about him, so it is like a court case.

phrases.aramaic: מִי יֵימַר דְּמִזְדַּקְּקוּ לֵיהּ הָנֵי תְּלָתָא.
phrases.english: Who says these three will agree to deal with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of why רבי יוחנן's rule does not apply to 'after I convert'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the outcome depends on others, so it is not 'in his hands'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a man can choose to convert, conversion might count as in his hands.
steps.terutzMaskana: Conversion needs three judges he cannot control, so it is not in his hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact definition of 'in his hands': the person must control the result alone, with no need for anyone else.

steps.title: Challenge from betrothing one's own maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks: if 'in his hands' is enough, then a master who betroths his שפחה 'after I free you' should also be מקודשת, since freeing her is up to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל objected: If so, take a man who gives a פרוטה to his שפחה and says 'You are betrothed to me after I free you'. Should that also be a valid betrothal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges רבי יוחנן's rule with a case where the man really does control the outcome by himself: freeing his own שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freeing his own שפחה needs no בית דין and no one else's agreement. So by רבי יוחנן's logic, the קידושין should work. The question assumes this result is unacceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (introduces a troubling result)
A small coin, the minimum for קידושין

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel objected to this:
If that is so,
one who gives a perutah to his maidservant
and says: 'You are betrothed to me
after I free you'
would that also be a valid betrothal?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'in his hands' rule on a case where control really is his alone.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that what is in one's hands counts as already done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Freeing a שפחה is fully in the master's control, so the rule would make this קידושין work, which seems wrong.

steps.title: A freed maidservant is a whole new person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: before she is freed, a שפחה cannot receive קידושין at all, and once freed she has her own mind, so his act now cannot bind her later self.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, at first she is like an animal, and now she has a mind of her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא בר ממל by showing that the שפחה case is different in a basic way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she is a שפחה, she has no ability to receive קידושין at all, the way an animal cannot. After she is freed, she is a Jewish woman with her own independent will. That change is so complete that the master's statement cannot carry over, even though freeing her is in his hands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בהמה' here does not insult her as a person. It means only that, in this legal area, she cannot receive קידושין at all.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, at first she is like an animal,
phrases.notes: For קידושין, a שפחה is like an animal: betrothal does not take hold on her at all.

phrases.english: and now she has a different mind.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: her basic legal status changes completely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since freeing her is in his hands, the קידושין should work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her change from 'like an animal' to a person with her own mind blocks the קידושין, whatever his control.

steps.title: Challenge from betrothing one's own wife after divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא ruled that a man who tells his own wife 'be betrothed to me after I divorce you' does not make her מקודשת. Since divorcing her is in his hands, should רבי יוחנן say it works?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רבי אושעיא's ruling: a man gives a פרוטה to his wife and says 'You are betrothed to me after I divorce you', and she is not betrothed. According to רבי יוחנן, should it be a betrothal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רבי יוחנן, using a known ruling of רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can give a גט on his own, so the divorce is in his hands. By רבי יוחנן's rule, the later קידושין should work, yet רבי אושעיא says she is not מקודשת. This case has no change in her basic status like the שפחה had, so the answer from step 3 does not help here.

keyTerms.meaning: But what about what so-and-so said?

phrases.english: But what about what Rabbi Oshaya said:
one who gives a perutah to his wife
and says to her: 'You are betrothed to me
after I divorce you'
she is not betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּהָווּ קִידּוּשִׁין?
phrases.english: Would Rabbi Yochanan say that this too is a betrothal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that the שפחה answer cannot handle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Divorce is in the husband's control, so the rule predicts valid קידושין, against רבי אושעיא's ruling.

steps.title: Divorcing is in his hands, but remarrying is not
steps.stepSummary: Divorcing her is up to him, but once she is divorced, betrothing her again needs her consent. So the later קידושין is not in his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that it is in his power to divorce her, is it in his power to betroth her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the step that matters, the later קידושין, is not something he can do by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule asks whether the thing that has to happen is in his control. He controls the divorce, but after it she is her own person, and he cannot make her his wife without her agreement. So רבי יוחנן's rule does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: In his hands, in his own control

steps.whatToRemember: 'In his hands' must cover the whole result. Controlling one step, like the divorce, is not enough if the final step needs someone else's consent.

phrases.english: Granted that it is in his power to divorce her,
is it in his power to betroth her?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what must be in his hands: the final קידושין, not only the divorce.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the divorce is up to him, the whole thing counts as in his hands.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remarriage needs her consent, so it is not in his hands.

steps.title: Trying to settle רב אושעיא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests using step 5's logic to settle רב אושעיא's open question: a man gives two פרוטות, one for קידושין today and one for קידושין after divorce. Since remarrying is not in his hands, the second should fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then resolve the question that רב אושעיא asked: one who gives two פרוטות to a woman. With one he says 'Be betrothed to me today', and with the other he says 'Be betrothed to me after I divorce you'. Resolve from here that it is not a betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the answer it just gave to settle an unsolved question of רב אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If remarrying after a divorce is never in the husband's hands, then the second פרוטה, given for 'after I divorce you', should have no effect. The question would then be solved: there is no קידושין after the divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised an unsolved question

phrases.english: Resolve the question Rav Oshaya asked:
one who gives two perutos to a woman,
with one he says to her 'Be betrothed to me today',
and with the other he says to her:
'Be betrothed to me after I divorce you',
resolve from here that it is not a betrothal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 5's reasoning to an open question.
steps.raayaObject: Answer to רב אושעיא's question: the second קידושין does not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of step 5: remarrying after a divorce is not in the husband's hands

steps.title: Her consent now may cover later too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: in רב אושעיא's case she agrees now, while single, so perhaps her consent covers both the קידושין now and the one after the divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, just as the betrothal takes hold now, it also takes hold afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 6 and explains why רב אושעיא's question is still open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5's case she was his wife, so she was not giving any fresh consent. In רב אושעיא's case she is single and agrees right now to both קידושין. Her present agreement may stretch to the later one, so the problem of needing her consent may not exist there.
steps.whatToRemember: The wife case and רב אושעיא's two-פרוטות case differ: a single woman who consents now may be able to agree today to a קידושין that starts after a divorce.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתָפְסִי קִידּוּשִׁין הַשְׁתָּא –
phrases.english: Perhaps, just as the betrothal takes hold now,
it also takes hold afterward.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתָפְסִי קִידּוּשִׁין הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof attempted in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the attempt to settle רב אושעיא's question; step 5's answer still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignored that in רב אושעיא's case she gives her own consent now, which may cover the later קידושין.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: attached produce can become תרומה once it is detached
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that תרומה cannot be separated between detached and attached produce. But if he says 'when they are detached,' and they are then detached, his words take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: You may not separate תרומה from detached produce for attached produce. If you did, it is not תרומה. How so? If he said, 'The detached fruit of this bed should be תרומה for the attached fruit of this bed,' or the other way around, his words mean nothing. But if he said 'when they are detached,' and they were detached, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's rule that something in a person's hands can be set up now to take effect later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce still attached to the ground cannot be part of a תרומה separation right now. Still, picking it is fully up to the owner. So if he says it should become תרומה 'when it is detached,' it works. This matches רבי יוחנן: if the later step is in your hands, your words today can take effect then.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Detached, already picked from the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not let attached produce become תרומה while it is still attached. The words only take effect at the moment the produce is picked.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַתָּלוּשׁ עַל הַמְחוּבָּר,
phrases.english: One may not separate תרומה from detached produce for attached produce,
and if he did separate it, his תרומה is not תרומה.
How so? If he said:
'The detached fruit of this garden bed'

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה זוֹ מְחוּבֶּרֶת״,
phrases.english: 'should be תרומה for the fruit of this garden bed that is attached,'
or 'The attached fruit of this garden bed'

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה זוֹ תְּלוּשִׁין״ –
phrases.english: 'should be תרומה for the fruit of this garden bed that is detached,'
he has not said anything.
But if he said 'when they are detached,' and they were then detached,
his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 6 was rejected in step 7, the גמרא brings outside support for רבי יוחנן's basic rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that an act whose later step is in one's hands can take effect later
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about separating תרומה on attached produce 'when it is detached'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows it even before the produce reaches a third of its growth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב goes further: even produce that has not yet reached a third of its growth can be made תרומה 'when it reaches a third and is detached.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said: Even if he said, 'The detached fruit of this bed should be תרומה for the attached fruit,' or 'The attached fruit should be תרומה for the detached fruit, when they reach a third and are detached,' and they reached a third and were detached, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds a bigger case: produce that is not even grown enough yet to need תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the only missing step was picking, which is in the owner's hands. Here a second step is also missing: the produce must first grow to a third. Growing is not in his hands, yet רבי אליעזר בן יעקב still says his words take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A third of full growth, the point where produce becomes subject to תרומה
His words stand; the statement takes effect

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Moreover, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said:
Even if he said, 'The detached fruit of this garden bed'

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה זוֹ מְחוּבֶּרֶת״,
phrases.english: 'should be תרומה for the fruit of this garden bed that is attached,'
or 'The attached fruit of this garden bed'

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה זוֹ תְּלוּשִׁין
phrases.english: 'should be תרומה for the fruit of this garden bed that is detached'
'when they reach a third and are detached,'
phrases.notes: These fruits have not even reached a third of their growth yet, so they are not ready for תרומה at all right now.

phrases.english: and they reached a third and were detached,
his words stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding a wider opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even produce not yet at a third of its growth can be made תרומה to take effect once it reaches a third and is detached.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף argue how far רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule goes
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits the rule to שחת, produce that has already grown stalks. רב יוסף says it applies even to אגם, produce that is still completely soft.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said this only about שחת, but not about אגם. רב יוסף said: Even about אגם.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how far רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the produce must already have grown real stalks, so it is clearly on its way. According to רב יוסף, the rule works even when the produce is still a soft, early sprout.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain that has grown stalks but is not yet ripe (used as animal fodder)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: רבה said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said this
only about שחת, produce that has grown stalks,
but not about אגם, completely soft produce.
רב יוסף said: Even about אגם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אֶלָּא בְּשַׁחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how far the ruling in step 9 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: only שחת. רב יוסף: even אגם.

steps.title: How do we know אגם means soft growth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word אגם refers to early, soft growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word אגם means early growth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where we learn the meaning of the word אגם. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אגם usually means a pond, so it is not obvious why it would describe a stage of plant growth. The גמרא wants a source for this meaning.

phrases.english: From where can we tell that this word אגם
is a word for early growth?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי אֲגַם לִישָּׁנָא דְּבוּצְלָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that אגם means soft, early growth

steps.title: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק: 'bow his head like a reed'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes ישעיהו, which compares a bowed head to an אגמון, a soft, drooping reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The פסוק says, 'Is it to bow his head like a reed (אגמון)?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אגמון is a reed so soft that it bends over. This shows that the root אגם describes soft, weak growth. That is the stage רב יוסף includes and רבה leaves out.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said: As the פסוק says:
'Is it to bow down his head like a reed?'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares a bent head to an אגמון, a soft reed, showing that אגם means soft growth.

steps.title: Whose view fits the ברייתא about betrothing an unborn daughter?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says betrothing a friend's future daughter means nothing. רבי חנינא says this is only when the wife is not pregnant, but if she is pregnant, his words stand. The גמרא asks whose view this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? 'If someone says to his friend, "If your wife gives birth to a girl, she is betrothed to me," he has not said anything.' And רבי חנינא said: This is only when his wife is not pregnant. But if his wife is pregnant, his words stand. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case about קידושין and asks how it fits the argument between רבה and רב יוסף. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby in the womb is like produce that has started to grow. It is on its way, so the words can take effect once she is born. The question is whether this matches רבה, who requires visible growth, or רב יוסף, who allows even soft, early growth.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case of

phrases.english: Whose view does this ברייתא follow?
One who says to his friend:
'If your wife gives birth to a girl, she is betrothed to me,'
has not said anything.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: And רבי חנינא said: They taught this only
when his wife is not pregnant,
but if his wife is pregnant, his words stand.
Whose view is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument of step 10 to a case of קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי חנינא's ruling fits רבה, רב יוסף, or both

steps.title: It fits both: רבה needs a noticeable pregnancy, רב יוסף does not
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, the case is when the pregnancy is already noticeable. According to רב יוסף, it works even if the pregnancy is not yet noticeable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבה, it is when her pregnancy is already noticeable. If it follows רב יוסף, it is even when her pregnancy is not yet noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא's ruling can fit both opinions, with each explaining it a bit differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A noticeable pregnancy is like שחת, growth you can clearly see, so רבה agrees there. An early pregnancy that is not yet noticeable is like אגם, soft early growth, and רב יוסף allows even that.
steps.whatToRemember: Something that has already begun to exist, like growing produce or a baby in the womb, can be the subject of words that take effect later. רבה requires that the growth already be visible (שחת, a noticeable pregnancy). רב יוסף allows even early, soft growth (אגם, a pregnancy not yet noticeable).

phrases.english: If it follows רבה, it is when her pregnancy was noticeable,
if it follows רב יוסף,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הוּכַּר עוּבָּרָהּ.
phrases.english: it is even when her pregnancy was not noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבָּה כְּשֶׁהוּכַּר עוּבָּרָהּ, אִי כְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling fits both: for רבה, when the pregnancy is noticeable; for רב יוסף, even when it is not.

steps.title: A second version: the argument is about watered fields
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבה says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule applies only to שחת in a rain-fed field. רב יוסף says it applies even to שחת in a field that needs watering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the argument went differently. רבה said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only meant fodder in a field that is not watered by hand, but not fodder in a watered field. רב יוסף said: even fodder in a watered field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the argument between רבה and רב יוסף from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, they argued about how grown the produce must be: שחת or even אגם. Here, both agree it must already be שחת. They argue only about a field that depends on watering. רבה says produce that cannot grow without watering does not count as having 'come into the world' yet. רב יוסף says it still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that is not watered by hand, which grows from rain alone
A field that is watered by hand and needs it to grow

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same argument from step 10, told a different way. In this version, nobody says the rule works for soft אגם.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov did not say his rule
except about fodder of a field that is not watered,
but about fodder of a watered field – no.
Rav Yosef said:
Even about fodder of a watered field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version of the argument given in step 10 with a different version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: only שחת in a rain-fed field. רב יוסף: even שחת in a watered field.

steps.title: Whose view fits the unborn-daughter ברייתא in this version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whose view fits the ברייתא about betrothing a friend's future daughter, now using the second version of the argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view fits what was taught: if someone tells his friend, 'If your wife has a girl, she is betrothed to me,' his words mean nothing. רבי חנינא said: this is only when the wife is not pregnant. If she is pregnant, his words stand. Whose view is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question from step 13, but now asks it about the second version of the argument. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pregnancy is like produce that is already growing. The question is which side of the argument supports רבי חנינא's ruling that betrothing an unborn baby works once the mother is pregnant.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand: the betrothal takes effect

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow, that which was taught:
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא from step 13. The גמרא asks about it again for the new version.

phrases.english: One who says to his friend:
"If your wife gives birth to a girl,
she is betrothed to me" –
he has said nothing.
And Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין אִשְׁתּוֹ מְעוּבֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: They taught this only when his wife is not pregnant,
but if his wife is pregnant –
his words stand.
Whose view is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second version of the argument against the ברייתא and רבי חנינא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Under the second version, which view supports רבי חנינא's ruling about a pregnant wife?

steps.title: When the pregnancy shows, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is about a pregnancy that is already noticeable, so in this version both רבה and רב יוסף agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about when her pregnancy can already be seen, and then everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a pregnancy that already shows, and both sides agree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, both רבה and רב יוסף require the produce to already be שחת, meaning visibly grown. A noticeable pregnancy is like שחת, so both agree it counts. Their argument about watered fields has nothing to do with this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Her fetus has become noticeable: the pregnancy shows

steps.whatToRemember: First version: רבה needs a pregnancy that shows, and רב יוסף does not. Second version: everyone needs a pregnancy that shows, so everyone agrees with רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: When her fetus was noticeable,
and it is everyone's view.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a noticeable pregnancy, which everyone agrees counts, just like שחת.

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים hold you can transfer what does not exist yet
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי, and רבי מאיר all hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי, and רבי מאיר all hold that a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a new statement. He groups three תנאים together because they share one principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the גמרא discussed one ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. אביי widens the picture: the idea behind that ruling, that you can transfer something not yet in existence, is also held by רבי and רבי מאיר. He will now show the source for each one.

keyTerms.term: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם
keyTerms.meaning: A person can transfer ownership of something that does not exist yet

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether you can transfer something that does not exist yet is a major question in the laws of buying, selling, and קידושין.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, וְרַבִּי, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, and Rebbi, and Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: all of them hold:
a person can transfer ownership of something
that has not yet come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, וְרַבִּי, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling to the general principle behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי, and רבי מאיר all hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.

steps.title: Sources: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, then setting up רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the source for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, which was already discussed, and begins the source for רבי from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: what we just said. רבי: as was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts proving each name on his list. For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, he points back to the ruling already discussed. For רבי, he is setting up a ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is his ruling about separating תרומה for produce that is still growing, which the גמרא just discussed. The proof for רבי is only introduced here; the ברייתא itself follows.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov – this that we said.
Rebbi – as was taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן. רַבִּי – דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving each name in אביי's list from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling discussed earlier on the דף, and a ברייתא about רבי that comes next.
